notes.maxzoom: z13 with 512 px tiles is about 5.8 m a pixel at 53 N; the national sources are 10 m (INFOMAR) and coarser.
notes.minzoom: z6 shows the coast's band on the all-Ireland view (the map opens on it at about zoom 6.3); z6-z9 are overviews (mean of the heights under each pixel).
notes.maxStationKm: A pixel further than this from every tide station in public/marine/tides.json has no tide to colour it by, and is left out. Northern Ireland's coast is on the site's own nine stations there (force5/ingest/tides_ni.py: Portrush and Bangor from the Environment Agency's gauges, Ballycastle, Larne, Portavogie, Killard Point, Ardglass and Dundrum Bay from EOT20), so nothing on the island's coast is that far now.
notes.polygon: A station with a polygon in stations.json (Strangford Lough inside the Narrows, Killard Point's tide 100 minutes later; fetch_national.BASIN_POLYGONS) takes every pixel inside it and none outside, whichever station is nearer (national.station_cells); the index carries the polygon, so a tap is read from the same region (areasAt in force5/src/foilDepth.ts).
notes.keepDeeperThan: EMODnet's cells that GEBCO fills are not soundings and are dropped (GEBCO drew Sandymount's drying flats 2-11 m deep), except where GEBCO has them deeper than this, twice the floor: those are deep water drawn as nothing, and the heights round them estimate the water between. EMODnet fills most of Northern Ireland's inshore water from GEBCO; with every such cell dropped, the sea a kilometre off the Antrim coast, 20-90 m deep, and round the Maidens was estimated from the beaches as shallow or drying.
notes.landDatums: A LiDAR in OD Malin or OD Belfast (`datum` MALIN or BELFAST) is brought to each pixel's own station's LAT with its stations.json odMalinOffsetMetres or odBelfastOffsetMetres. Northern Ireland's: at the Bangor and Portrush gauges, the Environment Agency's chart datum under OD (2.01 and 1.24 m, NTSLF's figures too) plus chart datum over the station's LAT; elsewhere the station's MSL less 0.166 m, MSL's height over OD Belfast at those two gauges.
notes.ceilingMarginMetres: Each region's dry ceiling is its station's highest predicted level over 2026-2028 (stations.json) plus this: three years are short of the 18.6-year nodal cycle by a few centimetres, and the waterline surface is good to about half a metre.
notes.pilots: The pilot areas of areas.json win where they are: their boxes are cut out of the regions at the pilots' min zoom and above, and left in below it, where the pilots draw nothing. Their merged grids (build.py --debug, which reach a little past the boxes) are the regions' most trusted source, so at a box's edge both archives hold the same heights.
notes.upperBeachMetres: The sea reaches up through ground that floods at a spring tide (MHW + marshAboveMhwMetres); above that, up to the dry ceiling, only this much upper beach beside it is foreshore. Fields and streets at 3-5 m LAT joined to the shore through a chain of low ground (behind Sandymount, round the Malahide and Rogerstown estuaries) are land.
notes.maxUnsurveyedKm2: Without the OSM mask only: unsurveyed water in stretches up to this size is drawn as such; a larger stretch is taken for deep.
notes.estimateMetres: Water no source gives a height (inside OSM's coastline) is estimated from the heights round it within this distance of one; further out it is drawn as nothing and a tap says it is unsurveyed. A distance under the chunks' margin (one z13 tile, 2.9 km), so every chunk judges a pixel alike.
notes.osm: OpenStreetMap's coastline (osmdata.openstreetmap.de's land polygons) and its tidal water are a hard mask (osm.py): outside them nothing is drawn, whatever a source says; inside the coastline nothing is land. Beaches, sand and marsh joined to the sea are drawn where a height says the tide reaches them.
